newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - BFS says Dime deal was best.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - BFS says Dime deal was best.

text.p: BFS Bankorp Inc, which has agreed to be acquired by Dime Bancorp Inc in a $92 million transaction, spoke to several suitors over the last few months and in the end decided the best deal for shareholders was selling out to Dime, President and Chief Executive James Randall said in an interview.
The two New York-based thrift companies announcd a definitive merger agreemeent late Tuesday.
Randall said in an interview Wednesday it was Dime's preference to do a cash deal although BFS would have been willing to look at a stock deal.
BFS holders will receive $52 per share in cash under terms of the agreement. The stock traded as low as 2-1/2 during the company's real estate woes in 1992.

"This was the best deal available," Randall said. He declined to identify any other suitors. He said he will be working on the transition for about six months and then will be looking for other opportunities which could be outside the banking business.

He said there is no overlap between Dime's branch system and the five branches of BFS, which operate as Bankers Federal Savings FSB. "I don't see any loss of jobs in the branches," he said. The senior jobs in the BFS headquarters will cease to exist after the merger is completed but Randall said some of the people may be offered employment in the Dime organization.

"From the first discussions with Jim Large (Dime chairman and chief executive) we found that Jim is someone extremely concerned with people, not simply out of benevolence but because he also recognizes that a key to the success of any company is the quality of people it has," Randall said.
Dime said in a news release Tuesday the transaction is expected to close in the second quarter of 1997.

Discussing his own job prospects, Randall noted that he is an engineer by training but after his experience with BFS he has become something of an expert in workouts of distressed companies, banking and New York real estate. BFS, once in financial difficulty, turned itself around by shedding non-performing real estate loans and through concentration on lending to the multifamily residential market.
As of September 20, 1996, BFS had assets of $643 million and Dime had assets of $19.7 billion.
BFS was advised in the talks by Keefe Bruyette & Woods.
BFS was up 1/2 to 51 in late trading and Dime was up 1/8 to 14-7/8.
